transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thanks for having me. Honestly, I’m not entirely sure where to start, but I guess... what really brought me in is that my mind just won’t stay on one thing anymore. It’s like, it's constantly bouncing around, you know? I’m a jeweler, I work with precious metals and stones, mostly custom pieces, rings, pendants, that sort of thing. It’s very detailed work, requires a lot of focus. But lately, I’ll be sitting at my bench, right? And I'll be trying to set a stone, or maybe I’m just filing an edge, and suddenly I’m thinking about a customer email I haven't replied to yet. So I go to check that, but on the way, I notice a saw mark on another piece I was working on yesterday, and I think, "Oh, I should buff that out really quick." And then, before I even pick up the buffing tool, I hear a noise outside—like a truck backing up or a dog barking, something completely random—and I’m looking out the window trying to figure out what it is. And by the time I turn back around, I realize I’ve completely lost the original work order. I can’t find the paperwork, I don't remember what I was even supposed to be doing with the first piece, and my whole bench is just a mess of half-started tasks. It’s exhausting, honestly, just trying to keep my thoughts in a straight line for more than five minutes. It never used to be this bad, but now it's just... everything grabs my attention all at once, and I can't filter any of it out.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Yeah, restless is definitely one way to put it, but it’s not just like... I don't know, tapping my foot or playing with my pliers, you know? It’s more like this intense, buzzing pressure inside my chest. If I try to just sit down and be still, like if I sit on the couch to watch a show or even just try to eat a sandwich, I physically can’t just *be* there. My brain starts screaming at me that I'm wasting time, and it turns into this massive need to just... accomplish things. Big things. 

Like, the other night, I was supposed to be winding down for the evening, but I couldn't sit still, so I just grabbed my laptop and my sketchpads. I started lining up all these new commissions, just firing off emails out of nowhere. And then I started messaging old customers, people I haven't made a piece for in two or three years, just pitching them ideas. And while I was doing that, I had another tab open and I was building a whole new plan for my website, mapping out all the galleries and the shop pages because the old layout suddenly felt completely useless. And then, at the exact same time, I was sketching out this whole Appalachian collection—like cast silver pinecones, oxidized twig rings, mountain-ridge pendants, the whole nine yards. I was doing it all at once, like I had to get it all moving right then, right in that exact second, or I was going to explode out of my own skin. So sitting still? I mean, I try, but it just turns into me trying to run a dozen different projects from my kitchen table all at the exact same time.
Are you finding it harder to meet deadlines or fulfill orders for your jewelry business because of these distractions and restlessness?

Oh, absolutely. It’s... it's been a disaster, honestly. I mean, I try so hard to keep everything on track, but it’s just slipping right through my fingers. Like, just last week, I had this massive custom delivery. It was a 25th-anniversary gift, a really intricate white gold pendant with a sapphire center and diamond halo. The guy had been planning it with me for months. And I had the stones, I had the cast ready, but with my brain just firing in a million directions, I kept starting it, then getting pulled into sketching the new website, then deciding I needed to reorganize my entire inventory of polishing compounds. And before I knew it, the deadline came and went. I completely missed it. The guy was furious, and I don't blame him, you know? 

And it’s not just that one order. My shop records... oh man, my records are usually so meticulous. I have a whole system for tracking invoices, material costs, client communications. But right now? It’s just piles of half-finished sketches and sticky notes with random ideas scribbled on them, mixed in with unpaid bills and loose gemstones. It got so bad, so completely disorganized, that I actually had to just put a freeze on everything. I put a notice up on my site saying I’m not taking any new work right now, which kills me because I need the income, but I just can't keep track of who paid for what or what I'm supposed to be making. 

And, you know, my family has noticed too. My mom and my sister, they’ve been calling and coming by the house way more than usual. They know I’m usually pretty disciplined—wake up at 7, in the shop by 8, you know, a solid routine. But lately, they’ll come over at 2 in the afternoon and I’m still in my pajamas, sitting on the floor surrounded by silver wire, trying to build a display case out of scrap wood while my actual commissions just sit there untouched. They’re really worried. They keep asking if I’m okay, saying I’ve slipped so far away from how I normally do things. And I tell them I’m fine, I’m just busy, but... I don't know, it's like I'm moving a hundred miles an hour but not actually getting anywhere.
Have you been making impulsive decisions, such as spending money or committing to projects without fully thinking them through?

Impulsive decisions? Spending money? No, no, not really. I mean, I know I just said I was sketching out all those new ideas, that whole Appalachian collection and reaching out to people, but I haven't actually *committed* to making them or, you know, buying the materials for them. Like I mentioned, I actually put a freeze on my website, so I'm definitely not committing to new projects from clients right now. If anything, I'm actively turning them away, which hurts, but I haven't been making promises I can't keep, aside from the ones that were already on the books. 

And as for money... honestly, I haven't been buying anything out of the ordinary. You know, with jewelry, the overhead can be absolutely brutal if you aren't careful. Silver is one thing, it's relatively cheap, but gold prices fluctuate constantly, and if you just go out buying stones willy-nilly—like, say you see a parcel of Montana sapphires. They are gorgeous, don't get me wrong, those teal and blue parti-colors are just incredible to work with, but if you buy them without a specific commission in mind, you're just tying up your capital for no reason. I learned that the hard way when I first started out. So I've always been pretty disciplined about my purchasing. 

Even now, with my brain going a million miles an hour and feeling like I need to do everything at once, I'm really just using the scrap metal and the wire I already have sitting around the shop. Like that display case I was telling you about, the one my mom caught me building on the floor? I was just building that out of old pallet wood that my neighbor threw out by the curb. I didn't go down to the hardware store and drop hundreds of dollars on oak or mahogany or expensive brass hinges or anything like that. I just pulled the nails out of the scrap and started sawing. So I don't really have the urge to go on a shopping spree or blow my savings. It's more just... the ideas, you know? The ideas are everywhere, and I want to do them all, but my wallet is staying pretty firmly in my pocket. I've always been a bit of a penny-pincher since I started the business right out of high school, you kind of have to be when you're bootstrapping the whole operation yourself, so yeah, no crazy spending or wild commitments like that. Just... a lot of chaos with what I already have.
Do you find that your emotions shift rapidly or intensely, such as suddenly feeling extremely angry, anxious, or sad?

Yeah, they definitely do. It’s actually been really jarring for the people around me, and honestly, for me too, because it’s like... it’s like flipping a switch, but I'm not the one holding the switch. 

Like, okay, to give you an example, a couple of weeks ago, I had a booth at this big artisan expo downtown. It’s a juried show, really hard to get into, so just being there was a huge deal for me. And after the show wrapped up for the weekend, I mean... I was just buzzing. I felt completely lit up. I was standing there looking at my display cases, and I just felt larger than life. I felt like every piece I had made was a total masterpiece, like I was finally hitting my true potential as an artist, and the energy in my chest was just glowing. I was on top of the world, just this soaring, incredible high. 

But then, literally in the blink of an eye, it would just turn into this intense, burning frustration. Like, my mom was there helping me pack up the velvet busts and the ring trays, and she made some offhand comment about how I needed to go home, get some sleep, and try to stick to normal shop hours that week so I wouldn't burn out. And I just snapped. I mean, I went from feeling invincible to just absolutely biting her head off right there in the middle of the convention hall. I started going off on her about how she was trying to stifle me, how she didn't understand the creative flow, and how asking me to slow down was like asking me to just stop breathing. 

And it wasn't just her, either. Anyone who even hinted that I should take a break or, you know, operate on a normal, boring human schedule, I would just lash out at them. It’s like this pure, soaring joy just instantly curdles into this really aggressive, defensive anger if anyone tries to put the brakes on me. It makes no sense to go from zero to a hundred like that, but in the moment, I just get so furious that they want me to be normal when I feel so extraordinary. So, yeah, the shifts are... they're intense. Really intense.
Have you noticed any changes in your personal relationships due to your recent behavior and emotional shifts?

I mean... yeah, definitely. It's... it's been really hard on the people around me, and I know that, even if I don't always admit it in the moment. Like I was saying about my mom and my sister coming over and checking on me... they’re just so worried, and I can see it in their faces. My mom, especially, she’s always been my biggest supporter, you know? When I decided to skip college and just dive straight into the jewelry business right out of high school, she was the one who helped me set up my first workbench in the garage. She bought me my first set of good jeweler's saws. So we've always been incredibly close. 

But lately... man, it's just strained. Like that time at the expo I just told you about, where I completely bit her head off just because she suggested I get some sleep. That really hurt her. I could see her just kind of shrink back, and she didn't say much for the rest of the drive home. And it’s not just that one time. It's like, every time she or my sister try to talk to me now, they’re walking on eggshells. They use this really careful, soft tone of voice, like they’re trying to soothe a wild animal or something, and honestly, that just makes me more irritated, which then makes me snap at them again. It’s this horrible cycle. 

And my friends... well, I haven't really been seeing them much at all. I used to go out with a couple of guys I grew up with, maybe grab a beer on a Friday night or go fishing out by the lake, but right now? I just don't have the patience for it. I feel like they’re all moving in slow motion, talking about, I don't know, football or their office jobs, and I'm just sitting there vibrating, thinking about all the things I could be doing back in the shop, all the designs I need to sketch out. The last time I went out with them, I ended up just talking over everyone, pacing around the bar, and eventually I just left without even saying goodbye because I suddenly had this intense need to go organize my polishing wheels. They haven't really texted me to hang out since then, and I can't say I blame them. 

So, yeah, it's... it's isolating. Even when I'm surrounded by people, even when my family is literally sitting on the floor of my shop with me, I feel like I'm on a completely different planet, operating on a completely different frequency, and it’s definitely pushing everyone away.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Weight? Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't actually stepped on a scale in... well, probably since I went to the urgent care for a sinus infection like two or three years ago. I don't keep a scale in the house, and I definitely don't have one down in the shop, unless you count the little digital gram scale I use for weighing out silver casting grain and gold scrap, but obviously I'm not standing on that! 

But no, seriously, just going by feel, I haven't noticed any changes at all. My clothes all still fit exactly the same. I wear these heavy canvas work pants when I'm at the bench, you know, just to protect my legs in case I drop a hot piece of metal or spill some acid or flux, and they still fit perfectly right around the waist. I'm using the exact same belt notch I've been using for the last year. 

And I'm still eating fine, you know, my mom will bring down a sandwich and just kind of leave it on the stairs for me, or I'll grab something from the mini-fridge I keep tucked under my secondary workbench. So even though I'm constantly moving around, pacing, hammering, filing, and my brain is just firing off constantly... my physical body seems pretty much exactly the same size. I haven't gained anything, haven't lost anything. So yeah, no weight changes that I'm aware of.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep at night?

Yeah, sleep has been... well, it’s been a total nightmare, honestly. And the frustrating thing is, I’m actually trying! Like, even when I force myself to leave the shop, go upstairs, scrub the polishing rouge off my hands, and get into bed at a totally normal hour—like, say, eleven-thirty or midnight, which for me is practically early—it doesn't even matter. I just lie there. I toss around for what feels like hours, flipping the pillow, getting tangled up in the blankets, just totally restless. My body is horizontal, but my brain is still running a thousand miles an hour. 

And then, if I do finally manage to drift off, it doesn't last. I’ll wake up way before dawn, like three or four in the morning, and my eyes just snap open. And instantly, my mind is just racing, fixating on work stuff, especially this missed delivery. I had this really important shipment of sterling silver casting grain and some custom-cut turquoise cabochons that was supposed to get here, and the courier completely botched it, and I just lie there in the pitch black, staring at the ceiling, obsessing over where that package is and how it’s throwing off my entire production schedule. I can't stop thinking about it. 

So by the time the sun actually comes up and I realize I'm definitely not going back to sleep, I have to literally drag myself up out of bed. And I don’t feel rested at all. Not even a little bit. I just feel heavy and drained, dragging my feet down to the kitchen to start the coffee maker, but my brain is still just spinning and spinning about that delivery and everything else I need to do. It’s like I’m running on fumes, but the engine just refuses to shut off, you know? So, yeah, falling asleep and actually getting any real rest... it's just not really happening for me right now.
Do you find yourself talking more than usual or dominating conversations?

I don't think so? I mean, I know I mentioned earlier that I was talking over my friends at the bar that one time, but I wouldn't say I'm dominating conversations or talking more than usual in general. It's more just that I have a lot on my mind, you know? Like, there's always so much going on in the shop, so many different projects I'm juggling, and when I get an idea, I just want to get it out there. But I'm not, like, monologuing at people or anything. 

Actually, half the time lately, I'm down in the shop by myself, so there's no one to talk to anyway! Unless you count me muttering to myself when a solder joint doesn't flow right, or when my torch starts acting up. Which, by the way, has been happening a lot lately. I think the regulator on my acetylene tank is starting to go bad, because the flame keeps fluctuating, and it's driving me absolutely crazy. You can't do delicate filigree work when your flame keeps jumping from a tiny pinpoint to a bushy mess. I need to order a new one, but I've been so fixated on that missing silver delivery that I keep forgetting. 

But anyway, to answer your question, no, I don't feel like I'm talking more than normal. I mean, my mom and sister might say I'm a little intense right now, but that's just because they don't understand the pressure I'm under to get this new line of rings finished. They see me pacing around and talking fast, and they think I'm losing it, but I'm just energized, you know? I'm just focused. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm dominating conversations. If anything, I feel like people just aren't keeping up with me. They talk so slow, and I just want to get to the point so I can get back to my bench.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life?

I mean, no? Not exactly like this. I don't think so. I've always been a pretty high-energy guy, you know? Like, back in high school, I was always the one who could pull an all-nighter before a big test and still go play a pickup game of basketball the next day without even needing a nap. And since I started working with metal, there have definitely been times where I get super into a project and just work for hours and hours without stopping. Like when I first learned how to do lost-wax casting, I was so obsessed with the process—getting the sprue just right, mixing the investment, the whole burnout cycle—I probably spent three days straight just casting little silver skulls and geometric pendants. 

But this... this feels different. It's not just being focused or having a lot of energy. It's like... it's like the volume on everything is turned all the way up, and someone broke off the knob. Even when I was really into casting back then, I still eventually got tired. I still eventually wanted to go to sleep, or hang out with friends, or just, I don't know, sit on the couch and watch a movie. Now, sitting on the couch feels like physical torture. My skin feels like it's buzzing. 

And the thoughts... my brain didn't used to race like this. It used to just be normal thoughts, one after the other. Now it's like five different trains on the same track, all going full speed, and I'm just trying not to get run over by them. Especially with that missing delivery—I swear, it's like a loop playing in my head. I've never been this fixated on something before. Usually, if a package is late, I just call the supplier, get an update, and move on to something else. But now, it's all I can think about. It's driving me crazy, and it's driving my mom and sister crazy, too, because I keep bringing it up. 

So, yeah, I've had times where I felt energized or really focused on my work, but I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. It's just... it's a lot. It's a lot all at once, and it doesn't seem to be stopping.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt similarly before, with this level of restlessness and racing thoughts?

Well, like I was just saying a second ago, no, not really. I mean, I know we literally just covered this, but to be completely clear—no. Not with *this* level of restlessness. I've never had my brain feel quite this... hijacked before. 

I mean, sure, there was this one time, maybe two years ago, right around Valentine's Day, which is obviously a massive nightmare in the custom jewelry business. I had this huge backlog of hand-engraved pieces, mostly these matching sterling silver bands that everyone suddenly decides they need at the absolute last minute, and I was working, like, eighteen-hour days at the bench. And yeah, I was stressed, and I was restless, and I was thinking about work constantly. But it wasn't... it wasn't anything like *this*. 

Back then, I could still, you know, sit down on my shop stool for ten minutes and eat a turkey sandwich without feeling like my skeleton was physically vibrating. And my thoughts were just... normal busy. Like a logical checklist. You know, "finish this ring, swap out the buffing wheel, polish that pendant." It made sense. Now, it's not a checklist at all. It's just noise. It's that missing courier package with the turquoise, and the acetylene regulator acting up, and the fact that people talk too slow, all just screaming in my head at the exact same time, overlapping each other. 

So, yeah, to answer your question again, I've never had a period where the racing thoughts were this loud or this out of control. Even when I've been swamped or obsessed with a new metalworking technique, I could always eventually turn it off. This time, there's just no off switch.
Have you ever felt an overwhelming sense of euphoria or an unusually elevated mood that lasted for more than a day?

Euphoria... I mean, I guess? If you mean feeling absolutely incredible and just buzzing with energy, then yeah, definitely. Like, right after this big jewelry and metal arts show we had downtown recently. I had spent weeks prepping for it, doing all this intricate bezel setting and polishing, and you'd think I'd be exhausted after standing at a booth for three days straight, right? I mean, most of the other vendors are practically dead on their feet by Sunday evening, packing up their velvet displays and complaining about their backs and their feet. 

But me? After the show, I felt... I don't even know how to adequately describe it. I felt completely lit up. Just lit up and larger than life one minute, like I could take on the entire world and forge a hundred new pieces before sunrise. I was riding this massive wave of inspiration, just completely elevated. 

But the frustrating thing—and this is what my family doesn't get—is how people react to that. Because I'd be feeling that amazing high, just totally larger than life, and then the very next minute, I snapped at anyone who asked me to stick to normal shop hours or slow down. Like, my mom or my sister would come down to the basement and tell me I needed to sleep, or they'd tell me to just work a regular 9 to 5 for once, which is a ridiculous thing to ask someone in a creative trade anyway. And I would just bite their heads off. I mean, I really snapped at them. 

Why would I stick to normal shop hours when I'm in the zone like that? Why would anyone in their right mind slow down when they have all that momentum? It's like they were trying to throw a bucket of water on a hot forge, and it just made me so incredibly mad. So yeah, I was definitely feeling elevated and euphoric, but also just... really quick to get ticked off if people were trying to drag me down to their level. Because to me, it's just obvious that when you're on a roll and feeling that good, you don't stop. You don't just pack up your torches and your pliers at 5 PM when you're feeling that lit up. You just don't.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Sleep? Oh, man, sleep has just been completely irrelevant lately. It’s actually kind of wild, because normally... you know, working with metal and stones, it takes a real physical toll on your body. You’re hunched over the bench peg for hours, filing, sawing, using the flex shaft, and usually I need a solid eight hours just so my hands aren't cramping up the next day. 

But lately? Not at all. I mean, for a while there, I was sleeping maybe... I don't know, two or three hours a night? Max. And you’d think I’d wake up feeling like a total zombie, right? Like I’d be dragging myself upstairs to make a pot of coffee just to barely function. But no, I’d open my eyes at, like, 3 AM, completely clear-headed. I mean, totally sharp and ready to go. I'd be so incredibly excited to just get right back to work that I couldn't even stay in bed if I tried. I'd jump up and head straight down to the shop to start cutting stones. I have this batch of rough turquoise and some fire agates I've been shaping, and I just couldn't wait to get them on the cabbing machine. 

Or if I wasn't cutting stones, I’d be up setting up my lightbox, taking all these macro shots, and posting all these new designs to my social media before the sun even came up. It’s honestly been fantastic having all those extra hours in the day to actually get things done while everyone else is just wasting time being unconscious. So, yeah, two or three hours, and I feel totally rested. Better than rested, honestly. I feel completely recharged.
How long have you been experiencing these racing thoughts and restlessness?

How long? Let's see... well, you know how I was just talking about that big downtown jewelry and metal arts show? The one where I had the intricate bezel settings? Well, what I didn't mention, which is actually really important to the exact timeline of all this, is that I actually won an award there. Best in Show for Metal Arts. It was for this massive sterling silver collar piece I did with inset lapis lazuli and a really complex hinge mechanism that took me literally months to engineer so it would sit perfectly flat on the collarbone. 

Anyway, they handed me that plaque on a Sunday evening as they were closing down the exhibition hall, and that’s exactly when it started. That’s when this whole... wired, completely out-of-control stretch really kicked off. 

From the second they announced my name over the PA system, it was like someone flipped a switch and the electricity just started surging through my veins. And that feeling, the racing thoughts and that intense restlessness where I couldn't sit still or stop working? That went on for about two solid weeks. Fourteen, maybe fifteen days of just pure, uninterrupted buzzing. 

I remember the exact timeframe because my buddy Dave kept trying to get me to come out and celebrate the award, like grab a beer and some wings or something, and I kept blowing him off day after day because I was just too wired to sit in a booth at a bar. I had to be at the bench, making things, using that energy. I couldn't just sit there and make small talk while my brain was going a million miles an hour. So yeah, to give you an exact number, it was a solid two weeks of feeling like that, just totally revved up and out of control, right after I got that award at the show.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable, and your thoughts were racing, and you had a lot of energy, that lasted for several days or longer?

Well, yeah, exactly like I was just saying about those two weeks right after the award. I mean, my thoughts were definitely racing, but it wasn't just in my head, you know? It was this physical thing, too. I had all this energy, and I just couldn't sit still. 

Usually, when you're at the bench, you have to be completely locked in, totally still, just focusing on one tiny detail under the loupe for hours. But during that stretch, I just couldn't do it. I'd sit down to work on a bezel, and two minutes later, I'd be up again. I'd bounce from sketching out this crazy new watch case design—like, a really intricate skeletonized dial concept I'd been dreaming up—and then suddenly I'd drop my pencil and start firing off emails to my gemstone suppliers in Jaipur, asking for quotes on bulk tourmaline. 

And then, before they even replied, I'd be over by my display cases, just completely rearranging all the velvet trays and the acrylic stands. And this would be going on at, like, 2 or 3 in the morning, long after I'd usually have closed up shop and gone to bed. I just kept moving, from one thing to the next to the next, like a pinball. I had so much energy I didn't know what to do with it all, so I just tried to do everything at once.

Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and your thoughts were racing, that lasted for several days or longer, and was so severe that it caused problems in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah, actually... yeah. It definitely caused problems. I mean, at the time, I felt like I was being incredibly productive, right? Like I was finally getting everything done that I'd been putting off. But the reality... the reality was a complete mess. 

See, I had this major custom delivery. It was an engagement ring, a really specific request—a platinum band with a tension-set Montana sapphire, and the client wanted this very particular hand-engraved scrollwork on the inside. It was a big deal, a high-paying job, and the guy was proposing on a specific date. And because I was bouncing off the walls, starting a dozen different projects and rearranging my shop at 3 AM, I completely lost track of time. I mean, I just totally blew past the deadline. The guy was calling me, furious, and I didn't even have the stone set yet. It was a disaster. I ended up having to refund his deposit and he went somewhere else, which is just... that's terrible for my reputation, you know? Word of mouth is everything in this business.

And it wasn't just that one ring. My whole shop... my records got so completely disorganized. Usually, I have a very strict system—intake forms, sketches attached to the work orders, a detailed ledger of materials used for pricing. But during those two weeks, I was just grabbing stones, melting down scrap silver, sketching on random scraps of paper, and not logging a single thing. I literally had to stop taking new work for now. I put a sign on the door and an auto-reply on my email because I have to spend, I don't know, days just trying to figure out what inventory I actually have left and whose repairs belong to who. 

And, well, my family noticed, too. They know how meticulous I usually am. My mom and my sister started calling and dropping by the shop a lot more. They kept saying they were just "in the neighborhood," but I know they were checking on me. They got really worried because they saw how far I'd slipped from my usual routines. I wasn't eating regular meals, my bench looked like a bomb went off, and I was just... I was talking a mile a minute about all these grand plans while everything around me was falling apart. So, yeah, it definitely messed things up. Big time.
Did you ever feel like you were on top of the world and nothing could bring you down during these periods of high energy and racing thoughts?

Yeah, oh yeah, absolutely. I mean, winning that Best in Show ribbon... it was like, I don't know, it just validated everything I'd been thinking about myself. Like I had finally proved that I was just on another level entirely compared to the other jewelers in the area. 

I mean, you have to understand, the metal arts community around here, it can be pretty cliquey, and a lot of people just stick to very traditional, safe designs. Basic prong settings, standard cast bands, nothing that really pushes the envelope. But I was looking at my work, looking at that sterling collar with the lapis, and I just felt this overwhelming sense of... invincibility, I guess? Like I was a genius. 

I honestly felt like I could take on literally every single custom order that came through the door—no matter how complicated, no matter what the client wanted—and turn each and every one into this absolute masterpiece, a total showpiece that no one else around here could even touch. I felt like my hands could just do no wrong, you know? Like every cut with the jeweler's saw was going to be flawless, every solder joint was going to flow perfectly on the first try. I was on top of the world. I felt like I was the best in the business, and nothing, absolutely nothing, was going to slow me down or prove me wrong.

Did you ever feel like you were so invincible or on top of the world that you engaged in activities that had a high potential for painful consequences, such as excessive spending or reckless behavior?

No, no, I wouldn't say I did anything like that. I mean, I know what you're getting at, like, did I go out and buy a Ferrari or, I don't know, gamble away my life savings or something crazy like that. But no, nothing like that. I mean, sure, I was feeling like a genius, like I said, and I definitely bought some extra materials—like I mentioned those tourmalines I was emailing about, and maybe a bit more silver casting grain than I strictly needed for that month—but that's just business, you know? That's an investment in the shop. 

I wasn't out there being reckless. I mean, I'm still a professional. Even when my head was spinning with all those ideas and I was rearranging the displays at 3 AM, I wasn't doing anything dangerous. I wasn't driving my car at a hundred miles an hour or getting into fights or blowing my rent money on something stupid. I was just... I was just completely consumed by the work and the ideas. 

I guess the worst consequence was just the disorganization and blowing that one deadline with the engagement ring, which, like I said, was a huge deal for my reputation, but it wasn't because I was out partying or spending recklessly. It was just because I was trying to do a million things at once right there in the shop. So, yeah, no excessive spending sprees or reckless behavior or anything that would physically hurt me or bankrupt me. Just... just the mess I made of my workspace and my schedule.
Did you experience any of these periods of high energy and racing thoughts for at least one week?

Well, yeah, it definitely lasted at least a week. I mean, if I really sit down and trace it back, the whole wired, completely out-of-control stretch started exactly right after I won that Best in Show ribbon at the regional metal arts expo. Which, by the way, was on a Sunday afternoon. I remember because I had to pack up my entire booth in the rain right after the awards ceremony, but I didn't even care about the rain because I was just buzzing so hard from the win. 

So from that Sunday, it just kept escalating, you know? The next day, Monday, I was back in the shop at dawn, and that's when the real frenzy started. The racing thoughts, the feeling like I could conquer the world, the starting a million projects and not finishing them, the 3 AM reorganizing sessions... all of that. And it didn't just stop after a few days. It just kept going and going. 

I'd say that whole period, that intense, non-stop energy where my brain felt like a motor running way too fast, it went on for about two solid weeks. Two weeks of just pure, unadulterated chaos in my head and in my shop. It wasn't until around the end of that second week, right around the time I realized I completely blew that deadline for the engagement ring and had that awful phone call with the furious client, that the bubble kind of burst and things started to shift. But yeah, for those two weeks, it was just non-stop, 24/7, full throttle. So, definitely longer than a week.
Did your period of high energy and racing thoughts last for at least four consecutive days?

Well, like I was just saying, yeah, it was definitely more than four days. I mean, if you're asking if it was at least four days, then absolutely, because it was a full two weeks. 

Like I mentioned, it all kicked off right after that jewelry show award. That Sunday afternoon, standing there with the ribbon, the rain coming down while I was packing up the display cases... that was the exact starting point. And from there, it was just this complete, wired, out-of-control stretch that didn't let up for a second. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday... those first four days were just a blur of me sketching out designs, ordering those tourmalines, tearing apart the workbench, and feeling like I was the undisputed king of the metal arts world. 

And it didn't stop on day four or day five. It just kept rolling right through the weekend and into the next week. It was a solid two weeks of that intense, motor-running-too-fast feeling before it finally crashed down around me. So, yes, to answer your question, it was way more than four consecutive days. It was fourteen days of just... non-stop overdrive.

patient.answer:
Oh, absolutely. It’s... it's been a disaster, honestly. I mean, I try so hard to keep everything on track, but it’s just slipping right through my fingers. Like, just last week, I had this massive custom delivery. It was a 25th-anniversary gift, a really intricate white gold pendant with a sapphire center and diamond halo. The guy had been planning it with me for months. And I had the stones, I had the cast ready, but with my brain just firing in a million directions, I kept starting it, then getting pulled into sketching the new website, then deciding I needed to reorganize my entire inventory of polishing compounds. And before I knew it, the deadline came and went. I completely missed it. The guy was furious, and I don't blame him, you know? 

And it’s not just that one order. My shop records... oh man, my records are usually so meticulous. I have a whole system for tracking invoices, material costs, client communications. But right now? It got so bad, so completely disorganized, that I actually had to just put a freeze on everything. I put a notice up on my site saying I’m not taking any new work right now, which kills me because I need the income, but I just can't keep track of who paid for what or what I'm supposed to be making. 

And, you know, my family has noticed too. My mom and my sister, they’ve been calling and coming by the house way more than usual. They know I’m usually pretty disciplined—wake up at 7, in the shop by 8, you know, a solid routine. But lately, they’ll come over at 2 in the afternoon and I’m still in my pajamas, sitting on the floor surrounded by silver wire, trying to build a display case out of scrap wood while my actual commissions just sit there untouched. They’re really worried. They keep asking if I’m okay, saying I’ve slipped so far away from how I normally do things. And I tell them I’m fine, I’m just busy, but... I don't know, it's like I'm moving a hundred miles an hour but not actually getting anywhere.

patient.answer:
Impulsive decisions? Spending money? No, no, not really. I mean, I know I just said I was sketching out all those new ideas, that whole Appalachian collection and reaching out to people, but I haven't actually *committed* to making them or, you know, buying the materials for them. Like I mentioned, I actually put a freeze on my website, so I'm definitely not committing to new projects from clients right now. If anything, I'm actively turning them away, which hurts, but I haven't been making promises I can't keep, aside from the ones that were already on the books. 

And as for money... honestly, I haven't been buying anything out of the ordinary. You know, with jewelry, the overhead can be absolutely brutal if you aren't careful. Silver is one thing, it's relatively cheap, but gold prices fluctuate constantly, and if you just go out buying stones willy-nilly—like, say you see a parcel of Montana sapphires. They are gorgeous, don't get me wrong, those teal and blue parti-colors are just incredible to work with, but if you buy them without a specific commission in mind, you're just tying up your capital for no reason. I learned that the hard way when I first started out. So I've always been pretty disciplined about my purchasing. 

Even now, with my brain going a million miles an hour and feeling like I need to do everything at once, I'm really just using the scrap metal and the wire I already have sitting around the shop. Like that display case I was telling you about, the one my mom caught me building on the floor? I was just building that out of old pallet wood that my neighbor threw out by the curb. I didn't go down to the hardware store and drop hundreds of dollars on oak or mahogany or expensive brass hinges or anything like that. I just pulled the nails out of the scrap and started sawing. So I don't really have the urge to go on a shopping spree or blow my savings. It's more just... the ideas, you know? The ideas are everywhere, and I want to do them all, but my wallet is staying pretty firmly in my pocket. I've always been a bit of a penny-pincher since I started the business right out of high school, you kind of have to be when you're bootstrapping the whole operation yourself, so yeah, no crazy spending or wild commitments like that. Yeah, they definitely do. It’s actually been really jarring for the people around me, and honestly, for me too, because it’s like... it’s like flipping a switch, but I'm not the one holding the switch. 

Like, okay, to give you an example, a couple of weeks ago, I had a booth at this big artisan expo downtown. It’s a juried show, really hard to get into, so just being there was a huge deal for me. It’s like this pure, soaring joy just instantly curdles into this really aggressive, defensive anger if anyone tries to put the brakes on me. It makes no sense to go from zero to a hundred like that, but in the moment, I just get so furious that they want me to be normal when I feel so extraordinary. So, yeah, the shifts are... they're intense. Really intense.

My mom, especially, she’s always been my biggest supporter, you know? When I decided to skip college and just dive straight into the jewelry business right out of high school, she was the one who helped me set up my first workbench in the garage. She bought me my first set of good jeweler's saws. So we've always been incredibly close.

I used to go out with a couple of guys I grew up with, maybe grab a beer on a Friday night or go fishing out by the lake, but right now? I just don't have the patience for it. I feel like they’re all moving in slow motion, talking about, I don't know, football or their office jobs, and I'm just sitting there vibrating, thinking about all the things I could be doing back in the shop, all the designs I need to sketch out. So, yeah, it's... it's isolating. Even when I'm surrounded by people, even when my family is literally sitting on the floor of my shop with me, I feel like I'm on a completely different planet, operating on a completely different frequency, and it’s definitely pushing everyone away.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has a history of similar episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about past history of similar episodes, which is not covered by any item in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I mean, no? Not exactly like this. I don't think so. I've always been a pretty high-energy guy, you know? Like, back in high school, I was always the one who could pull an all-nighter before a big test and still go play a pickup game of basketball the next day without even needing a nap. And since I started working with metal, there have definitely been times where I get super into a project and just work for hours and hours without stopping. Like when I first learned how to do lost-wax casting, I was so obsessed with the process—getting the sprue just right, mixing the investment, the whole burnout cycle—I probably spent three days straight just casting little silver skulls and geometric pendants. 

But this... this feels different. It's not just being focused or having a lot of energy. It's like... it's like the volume on everything is turned all the way up, and someone broke off the knob. Even when I was really into casting back then, I still eventually got tired. I still eventually wanted to go to sleep, or hang out with friends, or just, I don't know, sit on the couch and watch a movie. Now, sitting on the couch feels like physical torture. My skin feels like it's buzzing. 

And the thoughts... my brain didn't used to race like this. It used to just be normal thoughts, one after the other. Now it's like five different trains on the same track, all going full speed, and I'm just trying not to get run over by them. Especially with that missing delivery—I swear, it's like a loop playing in my head. I've never been this fixated on something before. Usually, if a package is late, I just call the supplier, get an update, and move on to something else. But now, it's all I can think about. It's driving me crazy, and it's driving my mom and sister crazy, too, because I keep bringing it up. 

So, yeah, I've had times where I felt energized or really focused on my work, but I don't think I've ever felt quite like this before. It's just... it's a lot. It's a lot all at once, and it doesn't seem to be stopping.
